# Language: Georgian (ka)

---

**Transliteration standard:** National System of Georgia (2002), as used in Georgian passports and official romanization, supplemented by standard academic convention for Georgian studies. Applied consistently throughout.

---

**1.**
**Form:** ჭეშმარიტი
**Transliteration:** č̣ešmariti
**Literal meaning:** root č̣ešmar- (truth, genuine substance) + adjectival suffix -i
**Typical English translations:** true, truthful, genuine, real
**Usage:** Used to predicate truth of statements, beliefs, and propositions. Also applied to persons to mean sincere or honest. Participates in productive derivation: č̣ešmariteba (truth, as abstract noun), č̣ešmaritad (truly, adverb).
**Epistemic status:** [CORE]

---

**2.**
**Form:** ჭეშმარიტება
**Transliteration:** č̣ešmariteba
**Literal meaning:** č̣ešmariti + nominalizing suffix -eba
**Typical English translations:** truth, truthfulness, veracity
**Usage:** The standard abstract noun for truth in philosophical, theological, and everyday discourse. Frequently appears in legal and moral contexts when the truth of testimony or a claim is at issue. Closely related to č̣ešmariti and shares its derivational family.
**Epistemic status:** [CORE]

---

**3.**
**Form:** სიმართლე
**Transliteration:** simartle
**Literal meaning:** si- (nominalizing circumfix, front part) + martal- (right, correct) + -e (back part of circumfix)
**Typical English translations:** truth, correctness, rightness, justice
**Usage:** One of the two primary words for truth in Georgian, often more colloquial or concrete than č̣ešmariteba. Used for factual correctness of statements and for moral rightness of conduct. The phrase simartle tkva ("told the truth") is highly frequent in everyday speech.
**Epistemic status:** [CORE]

---

**4.**
**Form:** მართალი
**Transliteration:** martali
**Literal meaning:** root martal- + adjectival suffix -i
**Typical English translations:** right, correct, true, just, honest
**Usage:** Applied to persons (a just or honest person), statements (a correct claim), and situations (a rightful state of affairs). Closely related to simartle and participates in the same derivational family. Commonly used in everyday moral and factual evaluation.
**Epistemic status:** [CORE]

---

**5.**
**Form:** სიყალბე
**Transliteration:** siq̇albe
**Literal meaning:** si- + q̇alb- (false, counterfeit) + -e
**Typical English translations:** falsehood, falsity, forgery, counterfeit
**Usage:** Denotes the quality of being false or counterfeit, applied to documents, currency, statements, and representations. Frequently appears in legal contexts involving forgery or fraud. The root q̇albi is borrowed from Persian/Arabic and is widely used.
**Epistemic status:** [CORE]

---

**6.**
**Form:** ყალბი
**Transliteration:** q̇albi
**Literal meaning:** borrowed root (cf. Persian/Arabic); adjectival form
**Typical English translations:** false, fake, counterfeit, forged
**Usage:** The standard adjective for counterfeit or forged items (q̇albi dokumenti, "forged document"; q̇albi fuli, "counterfeit money"). Also used for insincere or false behavior. Very common in legal and everyday contexts.
**Epistemic status:** [CORE]

---

**7.**
**Form:** ნამდვილი
**Transliteration:** namdvili
**Literal meaning:** na- (perfective/resultative prefix) + mdvil- (to place, settle, establish) + -i; roughly "that which has been established/settled"
**Typical English translations:** genuine, real, authentic, actual, true
**Usage:** The primary adjective for authenticity and genuineness of objects, persons, and states of affairs. Namdvili oqro ("real gold"), namdvili megobari ("true friend"). Widely used across registers and participates in productive derivation (namdviloba, "genuineness, authenticity").
**Epistemic status:** [CORE]

---

**8.**
**Form:** ნამდვილობა
**Transliteration:** namdviloba
**Literal meaning:** namdvili + nominalizing suffix -oba
**Typical English translations:** authenticity, genuineness, realness
**Usage:** Abstract noun derived from namdvili, used in legal, philosophical, and administrative contexts to refer to the property of being genuine or authentic. Appears in discussions of document authentication and in philosophical discourse about reality.
**Epistemic status:** [CORE]

---

**9.**
**Form:** სიცრუე
**Transliteration:** sicrue
**Literal meaning:** si- + cru- (lie, false) + -e
**Typical English translations:** lie, falsehood, untruth
**Usage:** The standard noun for a lie or falsehood in everyday and moral discourse. Contrasts directly with simartle. Used in moral condemnation of dishonest speech and in legal contexts involving perjury or deception.
**Epistemic status:** [CORE]

---

**10.**
**Form:** მცდარი
**Transliteration:** mcdari
**Literal meaning:** m- (subject preverb) + cdar- (to err, to be mistaken) + -i
**Typical English translations:** erroneous, mistaken, wrong, incorrect
**Usage:** Applied to beliefs, judgments, and statements that are factually incorrect or logically flawed. More neutral in tone than sicrue (it implies error rather than deliberate deception). Common in academic, scientific, and philosophical discourse.
**Epistemic status:** [CORE]

---

**11.**
**Form:** სწორი
**Transliteration:** sc̣ori
**Literal meaning:** root sc̣or- (straight, correct) + -i
**Typical English translations:** correct, right, accurate, straight
**Usage:** Used for factual correctness of answers, calculations, and statements, as well as for moral uprightness. sc̣ori pasukhi ("correct answer") is a highly frequent collocation. Also used geometrically (straight line) and morally (upright person).
**Epistemic status:** [CORE]

---

**12.**
**Form:** უზუსტო
**Transliteration:** uzusto
**Literal meaning:** u- (privative prefix) + zusto (exact, precise, from German/Russian borrowing) + privative construction
**Typical English translations:** inaccurate, imprecise, inexact
**Usage:** Used to describe statements, measurements, or representations that lack precision or accuracy. The positive form zusti ("exact, precise") is also common. Appears frequently in scientific, journalistic, and administrative contexts.
**Epistemic status:** [CORE]

---

**13.**
**Form:** ზუსტი
**Transliteration:** zusti
**Literal meaning:** borrowed root (cf. German genau via Russian точный influence, or direct borrowing); adjectival form
**Typical English translations:** exact, precise, accurate
**Usage:** The standard adjective for precision and exactness in measurements, translations, statements, and reproductions. zusti targmani ("accurate translation"), zusti monacemebi ("precise data"). Very common across registers.
**Epistemic status:** [CORE]

---

**14.**
**Form:** სარწმუნო
**Transliteration:** sarc̣muno
**Literal meaning:** sa- (circumfix front) + rc̣mun- (to believe, to trust) + -o (circumfix back); "worthy of belief/trust"
**Typical English translations:** credible, reliable, trustworthy, believable
**Usage:** Applied to sources, witnesses, evidence, and persons to indicate that they are worthy of belief or trust. Frequently used in legal and journalistic contexts. Participates in the productive sa-...-o pattern for "worthy of X" or "capable of X."
**Epistemic status:** [CORE]

---

**15.**
**Form:** დამაჯერებელი
**Transliteration:** damajerebeliˈ
**Literal meaning:** da- (preverb) + majer- (to convince, to make believe) + -ebel- (agentive/potential suffix) + -i
**Typical English translations:** convincing, persuasive, plausible, credible
**Usage:** Describes arguments, evidence, persons, or performances that are convincing or persuasive. Slightly more focused on the effect of persuasion than sarc̣muno, which emphasizes inherent trustworthiness. Common in rhetorical, legal, and critical discourse.
**Epistemic status:** [CORE]

---

**16.**
**Form:** გულწრფელი
**Transliteration:** gulc̣rpeli
**Literal meaning:** gul- (heart) + c̣rpel- (sincere, straight) + -i; roughly "straight-hearted"
**Typical English translations:** sincere, genuine, heartfelt, candid
**Usage:** Applied to persons, expressions, and intentions to indicate sincerity and absence of pretense. gulc̣rpeli bodiši ("sincere apology"), gulc̣rpeli grznoba ("genuine feeling"). Common in interpersonal and moral contexts.
**Epistemic status:** [CORE]

---

**17.**
**Form:** თვალთმაქცობა
**Transliteration:** tvaltmaqcoba
**Literal meaning:** tval- (eye) + t- (connective) + maqc- (to turn, to deceive the eye) + -oba (nominalizing suffix); roughly "eye-turning, deception of the eye"
**Typical English translations:** deception, trickery, hypocrisy, pretense, illusion
**Usage:** Refers to deliberate deception, pretense, or the creation of false appearances. Used in moral condemnation of hypocritical or deceptive conduct. Also used for visual illusions or sleight of hand in more literal contexts.
**Epistemic status:** [CORE]

---

**18.**
**Form:** მოჩვენებითი
**Transliteration:** močvenebiti
**Literal meaning:** mo- (preverb) + čven- (to show, to appear) + -ebit- + -i; roughly "of the nature of mere appearance"
**Typical English translations:** apparent, seeming, illusory, ostensible, spurious
**Usage:** Describes something that merely appears to be the case without actually being so. močvenebiti თანხმობა ("ostensible agreement"), močvenebiti safrtkhe ("apparent danger"). Used in philosophical, legal, and analytical discourse.
**Epistemic status:** [CORE]

---

**19.**
**Form:** ფიქტიური
**Transliteration:** piqtiuri
**Literal meaning:** borrowed from Latin/Russian fictivnyj; adjectival form
**Typical English translations:** fictitious, fictional, fabricated, sham
**Usage:** Used in legal and administrative contexts for fictitious entities, sham transactions, or fabricated claims. piqtiuri kompania ("fictitious company"), piqtiuri qidva-gayidva ("sham transaction"). A loanword with a narrower, more formal register than native alternatives.
**Epistemic status:** [CORE]

---

**20.**
**Form:** ავთენტური
**Transliteration:** avtentiuri
**Literal meaning:** borrowed from Greek/Latin authenticus via European languages; adjectival form
**Typical English translations:** authentic, genuine
**Usage:** A loanword used primarily in formal, legal, archival, and academic contexts to describe documents, texts, or artifacts of verified origin. Coexists with namdvili but tends to appear in more technical or international-facing discourse.
**Epistemic status:** [CORE]

---

**21.**
**Form:** სიყალბის დადასტურება
**Transliteration:** siq̇albis dadastureba
**Literal meaning:** siq̇albe (falsehood/forgery, genitive) + dadastureba (confirmation, verification)
**Typical English translations:** confirmation of forgery, verification of falsity
**Usage:** A fixed legal and administrative expression used in proceedings to establish that a document or claim is forged or false. Functions as a conventionalized phrase in legal Georgian rather than a free compositional description.
**Epistemic status:** [MARGINAL]

---

**22.**
**Form:** დადასტურება
**Transliteration:** dadastureba
**Literal meaning:** da- (preverb) + dastur- (confirmation, from Persian dastūr) + -eba (nominalizing suffix)
**Typical English translations:** confirmation, verification, attestation, authentication
**Usage:** The standard noun for the act of confirming, verifying, or authenticating a claim, document, or fact. Widely used in legal, administrative, and everyday contexts. The verbal form daadasturebs ("will confirm/verify") is equally common.
**Epistemic status:** [CORE]

---

**23.**
**Form:** გაყალბება
**Transliteration:** gaq̇albeba
**Literal meaning:** ga- (preverb) + q̇alb- (false, counterfeit) + -eba (nominalizing suffix); "making false/counterfeit"
**Typical English translations:** forgery, falsification, counterfeiting, fabrication
**Usage:** The standard noun for the act of forging or falsifying documents, evidence, or data. Frequently appears in criminal law contexts. The verbal form gaayalbebs ("will forge/falsify") is productive and common.
**Epistemic status:** [CORE]

---

**24.**
**Form:** მსგავსება
**Transliteration:** msgavseba
**Literal meaning:** msgavs- (similar, resembling) + -eba (nominalizing suffix)
**Typical English translations:** resemblance, similarity, likeness
**Usage:** Used to describe the degree to which one thing resembles another, relevant in contexts of authentication, identification, and aesthetic evaluation. msgavseba originaltan ("resemblance to the original") is a typical collocation in authentication discourse.
**Epistemic status:** [CORE]

---

**25.**
**Form:** არსი
**Transliteration:** arsi
**Literal meaning:** borrowed from Persian/Arabic asl (origin, essence); nominal form
**Typical English translations:** essence, substance, nature, core
**Usage:** Used in philosophical and analytical discourse to refer to the fundamental nature or essence of something. sakmis arsi ("the essence of the matter"), arsis mixedvit ("according to its essence/substance"). Common in legal reasoning and philosophical writing.
**Epistemic status:** [CORE]

---

**26.**
**Form:** შინაარსი
**Transliteration:** šinaˈarsi
**Literal meaning:** šina- (inner, inside) + arsi (essence); "inner essence, inner content"
**Typical English translations:** content, substance, meaning, purport
**Usage:** Refers to the actual content or substance of a text, statement, or legal instrument, as opposed to its form or surface appearance. Widely used in legal interpretation, literary analysis, and everyday discussion of what something really means or contains.
**Epistemic status:** [CORE]

---

**27.**
**Form:** სიზუსტე
**Transliteration:** sizuste
**Literal meaning:** si- + zust- (exact, precise) + -e
**Typical English translations:** accuracy, precision, exactness
**Usage:** Abstract noun derived from zusti, used to describe the property of being accurate or precise in measurements, translations, reproductions, and statements. Common in scientific, journalistic, and legal discourse when the degree of accuracy of a representation is at issue.
**Epistemic status:** [CORE]

---

**28.**
**Form:** უტყუარი
**Transliteration:** utyuari
**Literal meaning:** u- (privative) + tyu- (lie, deception) + -ar- + -i; "without lie, incapable of lying"
**Typical English translations:** infallible, indubitable, irrefutable, unerring
**Usage:** Applied to evidence, proofs, and sources to indicate that they are beyond doubt or incapable of deceiving. utyuari mtkicebuleba ("irrefutable evidence") is a common legal collocation. Carries a stronger epistemic force than sarc̣muno.
**Epistemic status:** [CORE]

---

**29.**
**Form:** მიბაძვა
**Transliteration:** mibadzva
**Literal meaning:** mi- (directional preverb) + badz- (to imitate, to copy) + -va (verbal noun suffix)
**Typical English translations:** imitation, copying, mimicry
**Usage:** Refers to the act of imitating or copying an original, relevant in aesthetic evaluation (of art, performance) and in contexts where imitation is distinguished from genuine creation or authentic production. Used both neutrally and pejoratively depending on context.
**Epistemic status:** [CORE]

---

**30.**
**Form:** გამართლება
**Transliteration:** gamarṭleba
**Literal meaning:** ga- (preverb) + marṭl- (right, just, correct) + -eba (nominalizing suffix); "making right, making just"
**Typical English translations:** justification, vindication, acquittal, excuse
**Usage:** Used in legal contexts for acquittal or vindication, and in moral and argumentative contexts for the justification of an action or claim. gamarṭleba sasamartloši ("acquittal in court"), qmedebis gamarṭleba ("justification of an action"). Participates in the productive martal- derivational family.
**Epistemic status:** [CORE]

# Language: Georgian (ka)

---

## Step 1 — Identify Central Roots

---

**Root 1**

**Form:** მართ- / marṭ-
**Transliteration:** marṭ-
**P1 participation:** 4 items — martali (#4), simartle (#3), gamarṭleba (#30), and the derivational base underlying mcdari (#10) via the contrasting cdar- root. Directly: martali, simartle, gamarṭleba, and the adverbial/prepositional form marṭo (see below). The root marṭ- (right, correct, straight, just) is the most productive native root in the truth-evaluation domain.
**Core meaning contribution:** Correctness, rightness, and justice — covering factual accuracy of statements, moral uprightness of persons, and legal vindication. The root spans epistemic, moral, and legal registers with high productivity.

---

**Root 2**

**Form:** ყალბ- / q̇alb-
**Transliteration:** q̇alb-
**P1 participation:** 4 items — q̇albi (#6), siq̇albe (#5), gaq̇albeba (#23), siq̇albis dadastureba (#21).
**Core meaning contribution:** Falseness, forgery, and counterfeit — covering the production and attribution of false or inauthentic items, documents, currency, and representations. The root is borrowed but fully integrated and highly productive in legal and everyday registers.

---

**Root 3**

**Form:** ჭეშმარ- / č̣ešmar-
**Transliteration:** č̣ešmar-
**P1 participation:** 2 items — č̣ešmariti (#1), č̣ešmariteba (#2). Fewer items than the other roots, but the root is the primary philosophical and theological vehicle for truth as an abstract property, and its derivational family is well-attested across registers.
**Core meaning contribution:** Truth as an inherent, substantive property of propositions, persons, and states of affairs — with stronger philosophical and theological weight than simartle or martali.

---

## Step 2 — Root Expansion

### Root 1: marṭ- (მართ-)

---

**1.**
**Form:** მართალია
**Transliteration:** martalia
**Literal breakdown:** martali + copula -a; "is right/correct"
**Natural English translation:** he/she/it is right; that is correct; you are right
**Context of use:** Extremely frequent in everyday conversation as a response particle or predicate, used to concede that an interlocutor's claim is correct or that a state of affairs is as described. Functions almost as a discourse marker in informal speech.
**Epistemic status:** [CORE]

---

**2.**
**Form:** მართალი ხარ
**Transliteration:** martali xar
**Literal breakdown:** martali (right/correct) + xar (2sg copula "you are")
**Natural English translation:** you are right
**Context of use:** Standard everyday expression for conceding correctness to an interlocutor. Ubiquitous in informal and semi-formal conversation across all registers and age groups.
**Epistemic status:** [CORE]

---

**3.**
**Form:** მართლა
**Transliteration:** marṭla
**Literal breakdown:** marṭ- + adverbial suffix -la; "truly, really, in truth"
**Natural English translation:** really, truly, indeed, in fact
**Context of use:** High-frequency adverb used in everyday speech to assert or emphasize that something is genuinely the case. marṭla moxda ("it really happened"), marṭla ar vici ("I truly don't know"). Functions as an intensifier and truth-asserting particle.
**Epistemic status:** [CORE]

---

**4.**
**Form:** მართლაც
**Transliteration:** marṭlac
**Literal breakdown:** marṭla (truly) + emphatic particle -c; "truly indeed"
**Natural English translation:** indeed, truly, in fact, as a matter of fact
**Context of use:** Emphatic form of marṭla, used to confirm or underscore the truth of a statement, often in response to a question or in conceding a point. Very common in both spoken and written Georgian.
**Epistemic status:** [CORE]

---

**5.**
**Form:** მართლაც რომ
**Transliteration:** marṭlac rom
**Literal breakdown:** marṭlac (indeed) + rom (subordinating conjunction); "it being truly the case that"
**Natural English translation:** it is indeed the case that; truly, the fact is that
**Context of use:** Used in written and formal spoken Georgian to introduce a concession or confirmation of a fact. Common in journalistic and analytical prose.
**Epistemic status:** [CORE]

---

**6.**
**Form:** სიმართლის თქმა
**Transliteration:** simarṭlis tqma
**Literal breakdown:** simarṭle (truth, genitive) + tqma (saying, verbal noun of tkva); "the saying of truth"
**Natural English translation:** telling the truth, truth-telling
**Context of use:** Used in moral, legal, and everyday contexts to describe the act of speaking truthfully. simarṭlis tqma valdebulebaa ("telling the truth is an obligation") is a typical moral formulation.
**Epistemic status:** [CORE]

---

**7.**
**Form:** სიმართლის დადგენა
**Transliteration:** simarṭlis dadgena
**Literal breakdown:** simarṭle (truth, genitive) + dadgena (establishment, determination); "determination of the truth"
**Natural English translation:** establishing the truth, determination of the facts
**Context of use:** Standard legal and investigative expression for the process of determining what actually occurred. Appears in court proceedings, journalistic investigations, and official inquiries.
**Epistemic status:** [CORE]

---

**8.**
**Form:** სიმართლის დამალვა
**Transliteration:** simarṭlis damalva
**Literal breakdown:** simarṭle (truth, genitive) + damalva (concealment, hiding); "concealment of the truth"
**Natural English translation:** concealment of the truth, hiding the truth
**Context of use:** Used in legal and moral discourse to describe deliberate suppression of true information. Appears in criminal law contexts and in moral condemnation of dishonest behavior.
**Epistemic status:** [CORE]

---

**9.**
**Form:** სიმართლის მოყვარე
**Transliteration:** simarṭlis moq̇vare
**Literal breakdown:** simarṭle (truth, genitive) + moq̇vare (lover, one who loves); "lover of truth"
**Natural English translation:** truth-lover, lover of truth, truth-seeking
**Context of use:** Used in philosophical, religious, and moral discourse to characterize a person who is devoted to truth. Appears in classical Georgian texts and in contemporary moral writing.
**Epistemic status:** [CORE]

---

**10.**
**Form:** სიმართლის მაძიებელი
**Transliteration:** simarṭlis madziebeliˈ
**Literal breakdown:** simarṭle (truth, genitive) + madziebeliˈ (seeker, one who seeks); "seeker of truth"
**Natural English translation:** seeker of truth, truth-seeker
**Context of use:** Used in philosophical and intellectual discourse to describe someone engaged in the pursuit of truth. More formal and literary than simarṭlis moq̇vare.
**Epistemic status:** [CORE]

---

**11.**
**Form:** მართლმსაჯულება
**Transliteration:** marṭlmsajuleba
**Literal breakdown:** marṭl- (right, just) + msajul- (judge, judging) + -eba (nominalizing suffix); "right-judging, just judgment"
**Natural English translation:** justice, administration of justice, judiciary
**Context of use:** The standard term for the justice system and the administration of justice in legal and constitutional discourse. marṭlmsajulebis sistema ("justice system"), marṭlmsajulebis ganxorcieleba ("administration of justice"). Appears in the Georgian Constitution and legal codes.
**Epistemic status:** [CORE]

**12.**
**Form:** მართლმსაჯულების სისტემა
**Transliteration:** marṭlmsajulebis sistema
**Literal breakdown:** marṭlmsajuleba (justice, genitive) + sistema (system); "system of justice"
**Natural English translation:** justice system, judicial system
**Context of use:** Fixed administrative and constitutional phrase referring to the institutional framework of courts, prosecutors, and related bodies. Standard in legal and policy discourse.
**Epistemic status:** [CORE]

---

**13.**
**Form:** მართლწერა
**Transliteration:** marṭlc̣era
**Literal breakdown:** marṭl- (correct, right) + c̣era (writing); "correct writing"
**Natural English translation:** orthography, correct spelling
**Context of use:** The standard term for orthography and correct spelling in Georgian. Used in educational, editorial, and linguistic contexts. marṭlc̣eris წესები ("rules of orthography") is a standard phrase in grammar instruction.
**Epistemic status:** [CORE]

**14.**

**Transliteration:** marṭlc̣eris c̣esebi
**Literal breakdown:** marṭlc̣era (orthography, genitive) + c̣esebi (rules, plural); "rules of correct writing"
**Natural English translation:** rules of orthography, spelling rules
**Context of use:** Standard phrase in Georgian language education and editorial style guides. Appears in grammar textbooks and official language regulation documents.

**Form:** მართლმადიდებელი
**Transliteration:** marṭlmadidebeliˈ
**Literal breakdown:** marṭl- (right, correct, orthodox) + madideb- (glorifying, praising) + -el- + -i; "right-glorifying, orthodox"
**Natural English translation:** Orthodox (Christian), Eastern Orthodox
**Context of use:** The standard Georgian term for Eastern Orthodox Christianity and its adherents. marṭlmadidebeliˈ eklesia ("the Orthodox Church"). Ubiquitous in religious, historical, and cultural discourse in Georgia.

**Transliteration:** marṭlmadideblobˈa

**Natural English translation:** Orthodoxy, Eastern Orthodox Christianity
**Context of use:** Abstract noun for the Orthodox Christian faith and tradition. Used in theological, historical, and cultural discourse about Georgian religious identity.
**Epistemic status:** [CORE]

**17.**
**Form:** გამართლება
**Transliteration:** gamarṭleba
**Literal breakdown:** ga- (preverb) + marṭl- (right, just) + -eba (nominalizing suffix)
**Natural English translation:** justification, vindication, acquittal, excuse

**18.**
**Form:** გამართლება ვერ მოხდა
**Transliteration:** gamarṭleba ver moxda

**Natural English translation:** no justification was found; acquittal did not occur; the action could not be justified
**Context of use:** Fixed legal and moral phrase used to state that an action or claim could not be vindicated or that an acquittal was not granted. Common in court reporting and moral evaluation.

**Form:** გამართლებული
**Transliteration:** gamarṭlebuli

## Summary of Derivational Patterns Observed

The following patterns are documented across the P1 set. These observations are drawn directly from the attested forms above and are not projected onto unattested items.

---

**1. Adverbial -ad suffix**
Attested productively across native and borrowed adjectives: č̣ešmaritad, namdvilad, marṭla (variant form), sc̣orad, zustad, piqtiurad, gulc̣rpeladˈ, marṭebuladˈ, arsebitad, šinaˈarsobiˈrivad. This is the most consistent derivational pattern across the set.

**2. Nominalizing -oba suffix**
Attested from adjectives: namdviloba, gulc̣rpelobaˈ, marṭebuloba, avtentiuroba, utyuaroba, damajereblobaˈ. Also attested from compound bases: marṭlmadideblobaˈ. Less consistently attested from privative forms (uzustoba: [UNCERTAIN]).

**3. Circumfix si-...-e nominalization**
Attested from roots: simartle (marṭ-), siq̇albe (q̇alb-), sicrue (cru-), sizuste (zust-), sisc̣ore (sc̣or-). This is a productive native pattern for forming abstract quality nouns, but it operates from roots rather than from the P1 adjectives directly.

**4. Resultative participial -uli**
Attested from verbal nouns: dadasturebuli, daudasturebeliˈ, gaq̇albebuli, gamarṭlebuli, gasc̣orebuli, dazustebuli. Consistently productive from preverb + root + -eba verbal nouns.

**5. Privative ara- prefix**
Attested: arasc̣ori, arasc̣orad, arasc̣muno, aragulc̣rpeli. Productive with native adjectives.

**6. Privative u-...-o circumfix**
Attested: uzusto (from zusti). Less productive than ara- in this set; only one clear instance documented.

**7. Agentive -eli / -veli suffix**
Attested: tvaltmaqci (from tvaltmaqcoba), mimbadzveliˈ (from mibadzva/badz-). Limited attestation in this set.

**8. Relational -obr-iv- suffix**
Attested: šinaˈarsobiˈrivi (from šinaˈarsi). Documented as productive in formal registers for forming relational adjectives from nominal bases.

## Overlapping and ambiguous items

The following items appear in more than one group or sit at the boundary between groups. The overlaps are noted without resolution, as they reflect genuine usage patterns rather than analytical imprecision.

---

**ნამდვილი / namdvili** — Appears in Group 1 (legal authentication of documents), Group 5 (genuine friendship, genuine feelings), and Group 6 (genuine artworks, genuine artists). The word is used across all three domains without apparent restriction, and the documented collocations span all three contexts. No single group captures its full range.

**ყალბი / q̇albi** — Appears in Group 1 (forged documents, counterfeit currency) and Group 5 (false smile, feigned feelings, false patriotism). The extension from documentary forgery to interpersonal inauthenticity is documented in P1b as a peripheral extension, but both uses are attested as [CORE]. The word thus straddles the legal-administrative and interpersonal-moral domains.

**ავთენტური / avtentiuri** — Appears in Group 1 (authenticated documents in legal and administrative proceedings) and Group 6 (authentic texts in philological and archival discourse). The distinction is primarily one of institutional context rather than meaning.

**სარწმუნო / sarc̣muno** — Appears in Group 3 (credible witnesses and evidence in legal and journalistic discourse) and Group 8 (through its derived form sarc̣munoebaˈ, which has shifted to mean "faith" or "religion"). The base adjective belongs to Group 3; the derived noun belongs to Group 8. The two uses are documented as semantically divergent.

**მართალი / martali** — Appears in Group 2 (factual correctness of statements: martali xar, "you are right") and Group 7 (moral uprightness of persons: martali adamiani, "a righteous person"). The word is used in both epistemic and moral evaluation without clear contextual restriction, and both uses are [CORE].

**სიმართლე / simartle** — Appears primarily in Group 3 (truth-assertion and truth-establishment) but also participates in Group 7 through the expression simarṭlis gzaze dadga ("got on the right track") and simarṭlis gamarjveba ("the triumph of truth"). The moral-rhetorical uses shade into Group 7.

**მოჩვენებითი / močvenebiti** — Appears in Group 6 (illusory aesthetic qualities) and also in legal discourse (ostensible agreement, apparent danger) that is closer to Group 1. Its primary documented use is as an analytical adjective for things that appear to be the case without being so, which cuts across both domains.

**ჭეშმარიტი / č̣ešmariti** — Appears in Group 4 (abstract and essential truth: true God, true faith, true knowledge) and Group 5 (true love, true friend) and Group 6 (true artist). The word is used wherever "genuine" or "true" is intended with emphasis on depth or fundamentality, regardless of domain.

**დამაჯერებელი / damajerebeliˈ** — Appears in Group 3 (convincing evidence and arguments in legal and investigative contexts). It is distinguished from სარწმუნო / sarc̣muno within Group 3 by its focus on persuasive effect rather than inherent trustworthiness, but both belong to the same broad context of evaluating claims and evidence.
